title: Scorify
tagline: Scorify is a challenge app where users create, share, and complete real-world challenges
description:
Scorify is an innovative platform that gamifies real-world experiences by allowing users and businesses to create location-based challenges for others to discover and complete. Businesses can use the platform as a powerful marketing tool by creating paid challenges, offering rewards, or simply increasing foot traffic and engagement with their brand. It also offers the potential to make crypto more useful in everyday life and more accessible to more people.

What makes Scorify truly unique is its integration with blockchain technology. Each completed challenge is immutably recorded on the Flow blockchain, ensuring that results are secure, transparent, and easily verifiable by anyone. This decentralized record-keeping enables users to prove their accomplishments, fosters fair competition, and helps businesses track participation and success rates.

Users can view challenges pinned on a map, participate in those nearby, and instantly see who else has completed them. This encourages community building and healthy competition. By bridging real-world physical activity with blockchain verification, Scorify opens new possibilities for engagement, advertising, and interactive entertainment.

In essence, Scorify transforms everyday locations into challenge hubs, empowering individuals and companies to connect in a fun, secure, and innovative way.
how_its_made:
Well... React Native isn’t compatible with the frameworks we used during the hackathon. The design is almost finished, but we couldn’t connect it meaningfully to any blockchain library. We tried multiple options—Flow, Yellow, LayerZero—but each time, we ran into issues.

After several frustrating moments where we just wanted to give up because of persistent errors, we decided to scrap the original plan. Instead, we quickly coded a small MVP overnight that hopefully captures a bit of the project’s vision. (./app in our github repo for our react native stuff, and ./scorify for our final vite result)
